test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 3 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three rivers whose interplay is responsible for the formation of the northern plains in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Godavari is the **second-longest river in India**, flowing for about **1,465 kilometers (910 miles)**.
 
• It originates from the Western Ghats near Nasik in Maharashtra and flows eastward across the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Godavari holds great religious and cultural importance in India.
 
• It is often referred to as the "**Ganges of the South**" and is a major pilgrimage site. Hence, its interplay is responsible for the formation of the northern plains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** [IMAGE: https://www.shutterstock.com/image-illustration/major-indian-rivers-on-map-600nw-2044555289.jpg] 

 
• **Ganga (Ganges):**

 
 
• It Originates in the Himalayas and flows through states like Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra:**
 
 
• Originates in Tibet and flows through Assam and Arunachal Pradesh in India before entering Bangladesh, where it merges with the Ganges.
 
 
 
• **Indus:**
 
 
• Originates in Tibet, flows through Ladakh, and then through Pakistan, though a small part flows through the northern region of India.
